$comment: DDL adapter for Claude Code (the protocol's implementations under hosts/claude/). The rule against mutation without approval always applies. From a prepared report or Git review in the record, a question carrying its ID, or a line-initial +++DDL_REPORT, until submitted human input, the gate guards only tool calls covered by PreToolUse; it reads no thinking block. Its catch-all matcher permits known safe reads, the gate's own report preparation, the prepared question unchanged, and bounded literal shell reads; mutating calls, unknown tools, worker follow-ups, and a question lacking the pending ID or differing from the prepared one are denied on those paths. The processor decides whether an actual submitted answer approves the current report and scope. Turn termination remains an instruction; running processes and hook-bypassing transports are outside this guard. The protocol's implementations under hosts/claude/ record the dispatch coverage and the human-input boundary; the asynchronous-transcript and fail-open limits are in the maintainer reference (Runtime boundaries). The spawn depth of 1 keeps worker starts with the lead. The hook acts only in a DDL project (an instruction file with the → DDL-PROTOCOL line) and there asks for the reviewed push (permissionDecision ask after the matched content review); whether that prompt appears depends on the active permission policy, and it is additional to approval in the /commit report. Commits carry no AI attribution. The rules live in the commands and protocol and remain instructions where the adapter is absent or cannot enforce them. Ordinary Git commit/push calls additionally require the prepared content review matched to the actual native submission and Git snapshot, even while STOP is open or native permission prompts are suppressed. An unreadable or mismatched Git review denies recognized calls. Runtime-level hook failures and timeouts remain outside that guarantee.
